page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs (2 threads per core) operating at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). The server is equipped with 84.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory allocation of 42.0 GB per core. It also includes 236 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The high 4.2 GHz clock speed drives top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2342.0 and strong single-threaded compression results, including 34.72 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, due to the limited physical core count, multi-core performance is weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score in the bottom 10% and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2884.0. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with large-block read and write speeds categorized as poor, though the Passmark memory score remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4-2mds_v2 offers an extremely high memory-to-vCPU density, making it a specialized choice for workloads that require massive memory capacity without the overhead of paying for unneeded CPU cores. However, the tradeoff is limited parallel processing power and lower database transaction throughput, as reflected in the weak Redis SET operations and Passmark database benchmarks. This server is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded or low-concurrency workloads, such as specialized in-memory caching, legacy applications with high memory requirements but single-core dependencies, and lightweight data processing tasks.
